title: What a Zscaler MCP tool result contains: full records, untrusted-content banners, JMESPath and CSV

untrusted-criterion.statement: A tool is flagged as returning untrusted content when a party without tenant credentials can author strings it returns; the dividing line is authorship, not the delivery channel, so device hostnames authored by an authenticated enrollee are not flagged.

quotes: # The test that decides membership: can a party WITHOUT tenant credentials
# author arbitrary strings that this tool returns? The dividing line is
# AUTHORSHIP, not the delivery channel
#   - zcc_list_devices / zdx device tools / zia device tools — hostnames and
#     device identity are authored by the IdP-authenticated enrollee

query-shapes.statement: An omitted or empty query returns the data unchanged; no match becomes `[]`; a scalar result is wrapped in a list; an invalid expression returns a single error record instead of failing the call.

csv-eligibility.statement: Automatic encoding sends a non-empty list of flat records as CSV; a non-empty nested value in any row disqualifies CSV for the whole response, which is then sent as JSON.

quotes: """A response is CSV-eligible iff it's a non-empty list of flat dicts."""
A NON-empty collection still disqualifies the row.
return isinstance(data, list) and len(data) > 0 and all(_is_flat_row(r) for r in data)
# AUTO: flat list -> CSV, everything else -> JSON.

csv-empty-collections.statement: Empty lists, dicts, tuples and sets count as CSV cells and are rendered as `[]` or `{}`, while an empty cell means `None`; before 0.15.0 a single empty list switched the whole response to JSON.

quotes: An **empty** list or dict counts.
if isinstance(value, (list, dict, tuple, set)): return len(value) == 0
return "[]"  # only reachable when empty; see _is_flat_scalar
return "{}"
An empty cell already means ``None``
a single empty list (such as the empty `urls` field on many records) switched the whole response to JSON

read-tools-trimmed-0-13-restored-0-14.statement: From v0.13.0 to v0.14.0 the server's read tools projected each resource down to a fixed subset of fields; issue #88 reported that `zcc_list_devices` returned only six device fields and had lost `policy_name`, and it was closed as completed when 0.14.0 restored the complete record and made field names exactly what the Zscaler API returns.

quotes: Since v0.13.0, read tools projected each resource down to a fixed subset of fields, so any attribute outside that subset silently disappeared.
Read tools now return the **complete record**, exactly as the Zscaler API provides it.
Field names in responses are now exactly what the Zscaler API returns
Starting with v0.13.0, the zcc_list_devices tool returns only a shaped, 6-field device summary.
The policy_name field
